correctness.rationale: The full symbolic proof was reconstructed: equality of burst outputs iff periodicity over the shifted interval, exact D_k formula, independent vertex-spin variables, even-degree subgraph expectation, one-lag forest binomial law, covariance orthogonality, graph decomposition by adding b modulo b+c, first-cycle threshold and positivity of the pgf excess. The first-cycle has exactly c/g b-edges and b/g c-edges. The final pgf correction is the only nonempty even subgraph at n0. The packaged direct enumeration covers 165 cases n=3..11 and checks every joint coefficient at each critical n, but is not relied upon as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The known deterministic burst-ball identity and one-shift binomial distribution are explicitly excluded from the originality claim. The new assertion is the sharp two-distinct-shift independence cutoff and its first nonfactorizing joint law. Full relevant scientific statements from Mercer, Schoeny et al., Xi et al., and three closest retrieved published results were compared, as well as an independently checked published-finding corpus semantic search. None read asserts or implies the two-width threshold. Residual risk is an unindexed equivalent statement in random autocorrelation/graph-cycle terminology.
residual_risks: An unindexed derivation under two-lag aperiodic autocorrelation statistics, cycle spaces or an Ising high-temperature expansion could cover the exact cutoff.
Search and reading can establish checked implication coverage, not absolute historical uniqueness.

value.rationale: In burst-deletion/synchronization modelling, two distinct burst widths induce two observations on the same random center. Although both counts have binomial marginals and identically zero covariance, their higher-order dependence begins at a sharp, gcd-controlled finite length. The closed first-dependent joint law reveals the exact deviation from independent modelling. This structural independent-to-dependent phase boundary answers a natural two-channel question rather than re-evaluating a standard one-channel mean or a finite arbitrary slice.
